# Oaks Data Analysis

**Name:** Kristen Brown

## Set Up The Data

### Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Import all the data

```{r}
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
```

## Summary Table & Data Cleaning:

### Height Data

#### Data Cleaning

```{r}
# This filters out 151 empty rows, all observations for dead seedlings, and all observations for NR seedlings.
Height_Data <- Height_Data_Raw |>
  filter(Data_Entered_By == "KB" | 
           Data_Entered_By == "DG") |>
  filter(Dead_Alive != "Dead") |>
  filter(Treatment != "NR") |>
  
  # Selects relevant columns and sorts the observations by tag number.
  select(Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, Notes) |>
  arrange(Block, Treatment)

# Oh no! The OS treatment was written in some rows as "OS", and other rows as "OA". I looked up how to use the replace function to make all "OA" values into "OS", and this seems to have worked:
conditions <- c("OA")
replacement_values <- c("OS")

Height_Data$Treatment <- replace(Height_Data$Treatment, Height_Data$Treatment %in% conditions, replacement_values)
# Phew! All "OA" values have been replaced with "OS".

# View the tibble to make sure cleaning works:
Height_Data

# Use group_by to know sample size for each treatment, for fun.
Height_Data |>
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  count()
```

#### Data Visualization

```{r}
# Boxplot of seedling height as a response to treatment.
Height_Data |> ggplot() + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = Seedling_Ht_cm, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_boxplot()

# Make a histogram graph to visualize the cleaned data
ggplot(Height_Data) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm), binwidth = 2)

# Histograms with facet wrap by treatment. This is where I first noticed that OA and OS were both used to describe OS (open space) treatment.
ggplot(Height_Data) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm), binwidth = 2) +
  facet_wrap("Treatment")
```

### Soil Moisture Data

#### Data Cleaning

```{r}
# This filters out 210 empty rows, 1 additional row with no soil moisture measurements, and measurements for the NR treatment.
Moisture_Data_Longer <- Moist_Data_Raw |>
  filter(Entered_By == "RK" | Entered_By == "NC") |>
  filter(VWC1_perc != "NA") |>
  filter(Treatment != "NR") |>
  
  # This selects the only columns I need and changes the VWC values from character to numeric.
  select(Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |>
  arrange(Block, Treatment) |>
  mutate(VWC1_perc = as.numeric(VWC1_perc), VWC2_perc = as.numeric(VWC2_perc), VWC3_perc = as.numeric(VWC3_perc)) |>
  
  # I am pivoting the table longer so that multiple VWC measurements per row do not exist. Every VWC measurement should have its own row.
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("VWC"),
    values_to = "VWC_perc"
  )  |>
  select(Block, Treatment, VWC_perc) |>
  filter(VWC_perc != "NA")

# View tibble. YESSSS it worked!
Moisture_Data_Longer
```

```{r}
# Create a summary table of average VWC_perc for block-treatment, which will be used to join with Height_Data.
Average_VWC_BlockTreatment <- Moisture_Data_Longer |>
  group_by(Block, Treatment) |>
  summarize(VWCmean_perc = mean(VWC_perc, na.rm = TRUE))

# View tibble
Average_VWC_BlockTreatment
```

#### Data Visualization

```{r}
# View VWC_perc column in a histogram
ggplot(Moisture_Data_Longer) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = VWC_perc), binwidth = 0.5)

# View VWC_perc column in a histogram
ggplot(Moisture_Data_Longer) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = VWC_perc), binwidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap("Treatment")
```

#### Join with Height

```{r}
# I want to join Height_Data and the Average_VWC_BlockTreatment moisture data. First I'll view them to see how I can do the join.
Height_Data
Average_VWC_BlockTreatment

# Now, I want to join the VWC_perc value from Moisture_Data to each seedling in Height_Data based on the seedling's Block and Treatment. 
Height_Moisture_Joined <- Height_Data |>
  left_join(Average_VWC_BlockTreatment) |>
  select(Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, VWCmean_perc) |>
  filter(VWCmean_perc != "NA")

# View the tibble for the new data frame.
Height_Moisture_Joined
```

##### Splitting the Blocks

Now, I want to create separate data frames for before and after the storm.

```{r}
# Create a new data frame for Blocks 001-004, for which data were collected before the storm.
Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm <- Height_Moisture_Joined |>
  filter(Block == "001" | Block == "002" | Block == "003" | Block == "004")

# Create a new data frame for Blocks 005-008, for which data were collected after the storm.
Height_Moisture_AfterStorm <- Height_Moisture_Joined |>
  filter(Block == "005" | Block == "006" | Block == "007" | Block == "008") |>
  filter(VWCmean_perc != "NA")

# View tibbles to make sure the filter worked.
Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm
Height_Moisture_AfterStorm
```

##### Visualization of Height-Moisture

```{r}
# Create a basic scatter plot for seedling height and block/treatment VWC, for Blocks 001-004 and Blocks 005-008.
Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm, y = VWCmean_perc) +
  geom_point()

Height_Moisture_AfterStorm |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm, y = VWCmean_perc) +
  geom_point()


# Same thing but with the axes flipped, for science.
Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWCmean_perc, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_point()

Height_Moisture_AfterStorm |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWCmean_perc, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_point()
```

Honestly, it's hard to tell from the scatter plots alone if there's any relationship between seedling height and soil moisture. The second set with soil moisture on the X and seedling height on the Y looks a bit more promising. I think there will be a relationship for soil moisture and seedling height for blocks 005-008, which were measured after the storm.

### Survival by Treatment

Lastly, for fun, I want to know how many seedlings survived and died in each treatment using the Height Data.

```{r}
# Create a new data object.
Height_Data_Survival <- Height_Data_Raw |>
  filter(Data_Entered_By == "KB" | 
           Data_Entered_By == "DG") |>
  select(Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, Dead_Alive, Notes)

# Do the process to replace "OA" with "OS" again.
conditions <- c("OA")
replacement_values <- c("OS")

Height_Data_Survival$Treatment <- replace(Height_Data_Survival$Treatment, Height_Data_Survival$Treatment %in% conditions, replacement_values)

Height_Data_Survival

# Use group_by to know survival counts of each treatment.
Height_Data_Survival |>
  group_by(Treatment, Dead_Alive) |>
  count()
```

Despite having taller seedlings (see ANOVA section), the open space (also called "open area") treatment also had the highest seedling death rate of the 3 manipulated treatments. The "SA" salvia apiana treatment is also included.

## ANOVA (Height-Treatment)

My question is: **Does treatment affect oak seedling height?**

My null and alternative hypotheses are:

- **H(null):** Treatment does not significantly affect oak seedling height.

- **H(alt):** At least one treatment does significantly affect oak seedling height.

Variables include oak seedling height ("Seedling_Ht_cm" - continuous, response) and treatment ("Treatment" - categorical, predictor).

### Assumption/Normality Tests

```{r}
# View the height data table and a boxplot and histogram of the data.
Height_Data

Height_Data |> ggplot() + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_boxplot()

ggplot(Height_Data) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm), binwidth = 2)
```

These seem normally distributed.

### Statistical Tests

First, I created a model and made a Q-Q plot, which looks fairly normally distributed.

```{r}
# Create the linear model
height_model <- lm(Seedling_Ht_cm ~ Treatment, data = Height_Data)

# Q-Q Plot
plot(height_model, which = 2)
```

The seedling height data looks normally distributed, so let's do the ANOVA:

```{r}
# Print the results to an ANOVA table:
anova(height_model)
```

There is a difference between at least one treatment, and I have an ANOVA table! Next I do a Tukey HSD test to see which treatments differ from each other:

```{r}
# Tukey Honest Significance Difference Test to see which pairs differ significantly from each other.

TukeyHSD(aov(Seedling_Ht_cm ~ Treatment, data = Height_Data))
```

So the seedling heights between OS and AC are different (p = 0.0073657), as well as OS and DT (p = 0.0338525).

### Figure

```{r}
# Create a summary table.
height_summary <- Height_Data |> 
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(Seedling_Ht_cm), 
            se = sd(Seedling_Ht_cm)/sqrt(n()))

# View the summary table.
height_summary

# Create a bar plot with the ANOVA results.
Height_ANOVA_plot <- ggplot(height_summary) + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill = Treatment)) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (mean-se), ymax = (mean + se)), width = 0.1) +
  geom_label(
    label = c("A", "A", "B"),
    position = position_dodge(0.9),
    aes(x = Treatment, y = 30),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3) +
  ylim(0, 35) +
  ylab("Mean seedling height (cm) ± 1 SE") +
  xlab("Microclimate treatment")

# View the ANOVA figure
Height_ANOVA_plot
```

```{r}
# Export the figure
png("ANOVA_height.png", units = "in", width = 5.5, height = 3.25, res = 300)
print(Height_ANOVA_plot)
dev.off()
```

## Regression (Soil Moisture-Seedling Height)

Okay, I decided to try this after all and to facet the regression tests and figures by date that the data was collected - before (Blocks 001-004) or after (Blocks 005-008) the storm.

My question is: **Are oak seedlings taller in treatments with higher soil moisture?**

My null and alternative hypotheses are:

- **H(null):** There is not a linear relationship between soil moisture and seedling height.u

- **H(alt):** There is a linear relationship between soil moisture and seedling height.

The two continuous variables are "Seedling_Ht_cm" (predictor) and "VWCmean_perc" (response).

### Assumption/Normality Test

```{r}
# Open the cleaned data frame for reference.
Height_Moisture_Joined

# Create histograms for each variable to assess normality.
hist(Height_Moisture_Joined$Seedling_Ht_cm)
hist(Height_Moisture_Joined$VWCmean_perc)

# Repeat the process for the Before Storm data.
Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm

# Create histograms for each variable to assess normality.
hist(Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm$Seedling_Ht_cm)
hist(Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm$VWCmean_perc)

# Repeat the process for the After Storm data.
Height_Moisture_AfterStorm

hist(Height_Moisture_AfterStorm$Seedling_Ht_cm)
hist(Height_Moisture_AfterStorm$VWCmean_perc)
```

```{r}
# For blocks 001-004 before the storm.
VWC.lm_BeforeStorm <- lm(VWCmean_perc ~ Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm)
plot(VWC.lm_BeforeStorm)
```

```{r}
# For blocks 005-008 after the storm.
VWC.lm_AfterStorm <- lm(VWCmean_perc ~ Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Height_Moisture_AfterStorm)
plot(VWC.lm_AfterStorm)
```

### Statistical Tests

```{r}
# For  moisture and height data from all blocks.
cor.test(~ VWCmean_perc + Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Height_Moisture_Joined, method = "pearson")

?cor.test

# Get the R^2 number
height_moisture.lm <- lm(Seedling_Ht_cm ~ VWCmean_perc, data = Height_Moisture_Joined)

summary(height_moisture.lm)
```

```{r}
# For blocks 001-004.
cor.test(~ VWCmean_perc + Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm, method = "pearson")

# Get the R^2 number
beforestorm.lm <- lm(Seedling_Ht_cm ~ VWCmean_perc, data = Height_Moisture_BeforeStorm)

summary(beforestorm.lm)
```

```{r}
# For blocks 005-008.
cor.test(~ VWCmean_perc + Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Height_Moisture_AfterStorm, method = "pearson")

# Get the R^2 number
afterstorm.lm <- lm(Seedling_Ht_cm ~ VWCmean_perc, data = Height_Moisture_AfterStorm)

summary(afterstorm.lm)
```

Okay, so none of these are great candidates for a linear regression. There's a higher chance of a relationship existing between seedling height and soil moisture in blocks 005-008 after the storm.

## ANOVA (Soil Moisture-Treatment)

### Assumption/Normality Tests

```{r}
# View the longer moisture data table and a boxplot and histogram of the data.
Moisture_Data_Longer

Moisture_boxplot <- Moisture_Data_Longer |> ggplot() + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = VWC_perc, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ylab("Volumetric water content (%)") +
  xlab("Microclimate treatment") +
  ggtitle("Soil moisture in all blocks")

Moisture_boxplot

ggplot(Moisture_Data_Longer) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = VWC_perc), binwidth = 1)

# Now do the process for just blocks 005-008 after the storm.
Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm <- Moisture_Data_Longer |>
  filter(Block == "005" | Block == "006" | Block == "007" | Block == "008")

Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm

Moisture_afterstorm_boxplot <- Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm |> ggplot() + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = VWC_perc, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ylab("Volumetric water content (%)") +
  xlab("Microclimate treatment") +
  ggtitle("Soil moisture in blocks 005-008")

Moisture_afterstorm_boxplot

ggplot(Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = VWC_perc), binwidth = 1)
```

### Statistical Tests

```{r}
# Create the linear model
moisture_model <- lm(VWC_perc ~ Treatment, data = Moisture_Data_Longer)

# Q-Q Plot
plot(moisture_model, which = 2)

# Repeat the process for just blocks 005-008 (I did this originally for blocks 001-004, and the ANOVA was insignificant).
moisture_model_afterstorm <- lm(VWC_perc ~ Treatment, data = Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm)

# Q-Q Plot
plot(moisture_model_afterstorm, which = 2)
```

```{r}
# Print the results to an ANOVA table:
anova(moisture_model)

# Repeat but only for blocks 005-008.
anova(moisture_model_afterstorm)
```

No difference in soil moisture (volumetric water content) between treatments for all blocks. Export the boxplot for potential use in the paper:

```{r}
# Export the boxplot figure for all blocks just in case I want to use it.
tiff("Moisture_boxplot.tiff", units = "in", width = 5.5, height = 3.25, res = 300)
print(Moisture_boxplot)
dev.off()
```

There was a difference in soil moisture between treatments, though, for blocks 005-008 after the storm. Let's find out which one(s) were different.

```{r}
TukeyHSD(aov(VWC_perc ~ Treatment, data = Moisture_Data_Longer_AfterStorm))
```
